title: Python Practice: Show Output
description:
Write a prompt asking Claude to write Python code that displays the message 'Level Up!' on the screen.

Do not look at your notes. Try to remember how output works in Python.
systemPrompt: You are a Python tutor. When given a task, write short Python code with a 1-sentence explanation. Keep it simple.
hints: Python has a built-in function that shows text on the screen. Its name describes exactly what it does.
The function name is print(). You put the text you want to show inside the parentheses, in quotes.
Example structure: print("your message here") — now write a prompt asking Claude to use this with 'Level Up!'

criteria: Did the AI use print() correctly?
Does the output show 'Level Up!'?
Is the code simple and correct?

title: Python Practice: Store a Value
description:
Write a prompt asking Claude to create a Python variable called 'lives' with the value 3, then print it.

Try to remember how to create a variable without looking at the lesson.
systemPrompt: You are a Python tutor. When given a task, write short Python code with a 1-sentence explanation. Keep it simple.
hints: A variable is like a labeled box. You give it a name, then use a symbol to put a value inside it.
The symbol you use to store a value is = (the single equals sign). Like: name = value
It looks like this: lives = 3 — then print(lives). Write a prompt asking Claude to do exactly this.

criteria: Is there a variable called 'lives' set to 3?
Is print() used to display it?
Is the code syntactically correct?

title: Python Practice: Do the Math
description:
Write a prompt asking Claude to write Python code that calculates how many minutes are in a day and prints the answer.

There are 24 hours in a day and 60 minutes in each hour. Try to figure out the code from memory.
systemPrompt: You are a Python tutor. When given a task, write short Python code with a 1-sentence explanation. Keep it simple.
hints: Python can do math using the same operators you know: +, -, and one for multiplication.
The multiplication symbol in Python is * (the asterisk). So 3 times 4 would be written as 3 * 4.
You need: 24 * 60 — put that inside a print() or store it in a variable first. Write a prompt asking Claude to do this.

criteria: Does the code multiply 24 by 60?
Is the answer printed (1440)?
Is the code correct and simple?

title: Python Practice: Make a Decision
description:
Write a prompt asking Claude to write Python code that checks if a player's score (set to 75) is high enough to pass (50 or above) and prints a message for each case.

Try to recall the structure from memory.
systemPrompt: You are a Python tutor. When given a task, write short Python code with a 1-sentence explanation. Keep it simple.
hints: Python uses a special keyword to check a condition. If the condition is true, it runs some code. If not, it can run different code.
The keywords are: if and else. After the condition, you need a colon (:). The code inside must be indented (4 spaces).
Structure: if score >= 50: / (indent) print('Passed') / else: / (indent) print('Try again') — write a prompt asking Claude to use this.

criteria: Is there an if/else checking score >= 50?
Are both branches printing a message?
Is the indentation correct?

title: Python Practice: Count with a Loop
description:
Write a prompt asking Claude to write Python code that prints every number from 1 to 5, each on its own line.

You should NOT need to write 5 separate print() calls. Try to remember the shortcut.
systemPrompt: You are a Python tutor. When given a task, write short Python code with a 1-sentence explanation. Keep it simple.
hints: Python has a way to repeat code automatically — you write it once and it runs multiple times. Think about the keyword that starts this.
The keyword is for. Combined with range(), it lets you count through numbers. range() generates a sequence of numbers.
Structure: for i in range(1, 6): / (indent) print(i) — this starts at 1 and stops before 6. Write a prompt asking Claude to do this.

criteria: Does the loop print 1 through 5 (not 0 through 4)?
Is range() used correctly?
Is there only one print() call (not five separate ones)?

title: Python Practice: Write a Function
description:
Write a prompt asking Claude to write a Python function called 'double' that takes a number, multiplies it by 2, and returns the result. Then call it with the number 7 and print the output.

Try this from memory.
systemPrompt: You are a Python tutor. When given a task, write short Python code with a 1-sentence explanation. Keep it simple.
hints: To create a reusable block of code in Python, you use a specific keyword followed by a name and parentheses. The code inside is indented.
The keyword is def. So: def function_name(parameter): — then the indented code runs when you call it. Use return to send a value back.
Structure: def double(n): / (indent) return n * 2 / (blank line) / print(double(7)) — write a prompt asking Claude to write exactly this.

criteria: Is there a function called 'double' that accepts one parameter?
Does it multiply the parameter by 2 and return the result?
Is it called with 7 and the result printed?

title: JS Practice: Show Output
description:
Write a prompt asking Claude to write JavaScript code that displays the message 'Player Ready!' in the console.

Try to recall the JavaScript way to show output without looking at your notes.
systemPrompt: You are a JavaScript tutor. When given a task, write short JavaScript code with a 1-sentence explanation. Keep it simple.
hints: JavaScript output goes to the browser's developer console. There is a built-in object with a method for logging output.
The object is called console. The method is .log(). You call them together: console.log()
Structure: console.log("Player Ready!"); — note the semicolon at the end. Write a prompt asking Claude to write this.

criteria: Does the code use console.log()?
Does it output 'Player Ready!'?
Is the semicolon present?

title: JS Practice: Create Variables
description:
Write a prompt asking Claude to write JavaScript that stores a player's name in a variable that won't change, and a player's score in a variable that can change. Then add 50 to the score and log both variables.

Remember the two different variable keywords and when to use each.
systemPrompt: You are a JavaScript tutor. When given a task, write short JavaScript code with a 1-sentence explanation. Keep it simple.
hints: JavaScript has two modern ways to create variables. One is for values that never change. One is for values that might change later.
Use const for things that stay the same. Use let for things that will be updated. Avoid var — it is older and causes confusion.
Structure: const name = "Alex"; / let score = 0; / score = score + 50; / console.log(name, score); — write a prompt for this.

criteria: Is const used for the name and let for the score?
Is 50 added to the score?
Are both variables logged?

title: JS Practice: Make a Decision
description:
Write a prompt asking Claude to write JavaScript that checks if a temperature variable (set to 95) is above 90. If it is, log 'Stay hydrated!' Otherwise, log 'Enjoy the weather!'

Remember the JavaScript syntax is slightly different from Python.
systemPrompt: You are a JavaScript tutor. When given a task, write short JavaScript code with a 1-sentence explanation. Keep it simple.
hints: JavaScript uses if and else just like Python. The main difference is how you write the condition and the code block.
In JavaScript: the condition goes inside ( ) and the code block goes inside { }. No indentation requirement — the curly braces do the job.
Structure: if (temperature > 90) { / console.log('Stay hydrated!'); / } else { / console.log('Enjoy the weather!'); / } — write a prompt for this.

criteria: Is the condition checking temperature > 90?
Are parentheses () used for the condition?
Are curly braces {} used for the code blocks?

title: JS Practice: Count with a Loop
description:
Write a prompt asking Claude to write JavaScript that logs the numbers 1 through 5 using a loop.

Remember: JavaScript for loops look a bit more verbose than Python's. Try to recall all 3 parts.
systemPrompt: You are a JavaScript tutor. When given a task, write short JavaScript code with a 1-sentence explanation. Keep it simple.
hints: A JavaScript for loop has 3 parts inside the parentheses, separated by semicolons: a starting point, a condition to keep going, and an update step.
The 3 parts are: let i = 1 (start at 1), i <= 5 (keep going while i is 5 or less), i++ (add 1 each time).
Structure: for (let i = 1; i <= 5; i++) { / console.log(i); / } — write a prompt asking Claude to write exactly this.

criteria: Does the loop output 1 through 5?
Does it use correct for loop syntax with all 3 parts?
Is console.log() used inside the loop?

title: JS Practice: Write a Function
description:
Write a prompt asking Claude to write a JavaScript function called 'greet' that takes a name as input and logs 'Hello, [name]!' when called. Then call it with any name.

Try to remember the function syntax from memory.
systemPrompt: You are a JavaScript tutor. When given a task, write short JavaScript code with a 1-sentence explanation. Keep it simple.
hints: In JavaScript, to define a reusable block of code, you use a specific keyword followed by a name and parentheses. The code goes in curly braces.
The keyword is function. To pass information in, you put a parameter name inside the (). To build the message, use a template literal with backticks.
Structure: function greet(name) { / console.log(`Hello, ${name}!`); / } / greet("Sam"); — write a prompt asking Claude to write this.

criteria: Is there a function called 'greet' with one parameter?
Does it log a greeting that includes the name?
Is the function called with a test name?

title: JS Practice: Work with an Array
description:
Write a prompt asking Claude to write JavaScript that creates an array of 3 colors, then logs each color using a loop.

See if you can remember both how to make the array and how to loop through it.
systemPrompt: You are a JavaScript tutor. When given a task, write short JavaScript code with a 1-sentence explanation. Keep it simple.
hints: An array in JavaScript holds multiple items in one variable. The items go inside square brackets, separated by commas.
To loop through an array, you can use .forEach(). It runs a function once for each item. The function receives the current item as a parameter.
Structure: const colors = ["red", "blue", "green"]; / colors.forEach(function(color) { / console.log(color); / }); — write a prompt for this.

criteria: Is there an array with 3 colors?
Does the loop go through each item?
Is each color logged separately?
